residency.test: The ordinary concepts test, plus the domicile, 183-day and Commonwealth superannuation tests. Meeting any statutory test makes you resident.
residency.worldwide_income: Yes for residents. Non-residents pay from the first dollar at 30% with no tax-free threshold and no Medicare levy.
residency.note: The tax year runs 1 July to 30 June. Figures here are for the 2025-26 year.
residency.temporary_resident: Holders of certain temporary visas are exempt from Australian tax on most foreign income.

surcharges.name: Medicare levy
surcharges.note: phased in between 27,222 and 34,027; family thresholds are higher

surcharges.name: Medicare levy surcharge
surcharges.note: only if you have no eligible private hospital cover; rises to 1.25% and 1.5% at higher income tiers

credits.name: Low income tax offset
credits.note: reduces at 5c per dollar to 45,000 then 1.5c per dollar to 66,667

employer.name: Superannuation guarantee
employer.note: 12% from 1 July 2025, subject to the maximum contribution base

capital_gains.discount: 50% CGT discount on assets held more than 12 months by individuals
capital_gains.rate: net gains are added to income and taxed at marginal rates
capital_gains.principal_residence: the main residence exemption generally applies, but is lost for foreign residents at the time of sale
capital_gains.note: there is no separate CGT rate - the discount is the relief mechanism

quirks: The tax year ends 30 June. Anyone arriving from a calendar-year country routinely gets this wrong on their first return.
The Medicare levy surcharge means that for many people earning above about 101,000, buying basic private hospital cover costs less than the surcharge they avoid.
HELP/HECS student loan repayments are collected through the tax system and are calculated on repayment income, which adds back reportable fringe benefits and salary-sacrificed super.
Salary-sacrificed superannuation is taxed at 15% inside the fund, well below most marginal rates, up to the 30,000 concessional cap.
Foreign residents lose the tax-free threshold entirely and pay 30% from the first dollar.

reporting.portal: https://my.gov.au linked to ATO online services
reporting.who_must_file: Most residents with income above the tax-free threshold, anyone who had tax withheld, and anyone carrying on a business regardless of profit.

deadlines.what: Individual return for the 2025-26 year if you lodge yourself
Extended deadline if lodging through a registered tax agent
deadlines.note: you must be on the agent's client list before 31 October

deadlines.what: Business activity statement (BAS) for GST and PAYG instalments
Employers finalise Single Touch Payroll so income statements become tax-ready

forms.name: Lodged through myTax, an agent, or paper
Replaces the old payment summary; delivered via Single Touch Payroll
Business and professional items schedule for sole traders
Business activity statement for GST-registered taxpayers
Given to each employer when starting work

documents_to_collect: Income statements from all employers (usually pre-filled by mid-July)
Private health insurance statement - needed to avoid the surcharge
Records of work-related deductions: car logbook, home office hours, professional subscriptions, self-education
Rental property income and expense records including depreciation schedules

penalties.failure_to_lodge: one penalty unit per 28 days late, up to five units
penalties.shortfall: 25% to 75% of the shortfall depending on behaviour

warnings: HELP/HECS student loan repayments are not modelled and can add up to 10% of repayment income.
The Medicare levy phase-in range and family thresholds are simplified.
Superannuation is shown as an employer cost; it is not withheld from the employee's salary.
